title: Implement shadow simulated order matching quote slippage and costs
description:
Implement the shadow order-matching simulator in mike_trade/brokers/shadow/fills.py. It turns pending SHADOW market and limit orders into estimated fills using contemporaneous quote data from the shared market-data snapshot. It never calls a broker.

Rules:
- Buys fill against the ask and sells against the bid.
- Configurable latency: only quotes whose timestamp is at or after order time plus latency are eligible.
- Configurable slippage in bps and/or ticks. It always moves the price against the trader.
- Configurable fee model.
- Liquidity participation/size policy: a fill can be at most a configured fraction of the displayed bid/ask size. The remainder stays pending, producing a partial fill, only where size evidence supports it.
- Limit orders fill only when the opposing quote crosses the limit, at the better of the limit and the quote plus slippage, never better than the quote.
- Regular-session-only restriction, using the exchange calendar in America/New_York.
- Whole versus fractional precision policy. Unsupported fractional/order-type combinations fail closed.
- Never fill at a candle close merely because a bar crossed. A bar without a quote is not fill evidence.
- When quotes are missing, stale beyond a configured threshold, crossed/locked, have zero size, or otherwise cannot support a confident fill, produce no fill or an explicit UNCERTAIN outcome with a reason. Never fabricate a price.

Every fill result records the simulator version, the assumptions used (latency, slippage, participation, fee), the quote timestamp/price/size used, and feed provenance (for example IEX, not consolidated SIP). It is labeled estimated and not broker-confirmed. Fills are applied to ShadowAccount/ShadowLedger from p.1. That layer remains the authority for the cash/no-negative-cash and no-short checks. All prices, quantities and fees are Decimal, and times are UTC-aware.

Before editing, inspect:
- mike_trade/brokers/shadow/account.py and mike_trade/brokers/shadow/ledger.py (from p.1)
- existing quote/market-snapshot types and IEX provenance fields in the shared market-data service under mike_trade/
- existing order types, the order-capability/fractional policy, and the exchange session calendar utilities

Write tests/unit/test_shadow_fills.py covering both positive and negative cases.
acceptance_criteria: Market buy fills at ask plus slippage and market sell fills at bid minus slippage, with exact Decimal equality asserted in tests
Quotes timestamped before order time plus configured latency are not used for fills
A limit buy does not fill while ask > limit and fills when ask <= limit, at a price never better than the quote; the symmetric case is tested for a limit sell
With participation cap p and displayed size s, the filled quantity is <= p*s and the remainder stays pending as a partial fill
Missing, stale, crossed/locked or zero-size quotes produce no fill or an UNCERTAIN outcome with a recorded reason, never a fabricated price
A completed bar crossing a limit price without supporting quote evidence produces no fill (candle close is never used as the fill price)
Orders outside regular session hours are not filled when the session restriction is enabled
An unsupported fractional/order-type combination is rejected fail-closed
Each fill record includes simulator version, assumptions, quote evidence, feed provenance, estimated=True and broker_confirmed=False
Fees are deducted exactly, and a fill that would make cash negative (margin disabled) is rejected via the account layer
The module imports no Alpaca trading client or broker credential configuration
tests/unit/test_shadow_fills.py exists with positive and negative tests and passes when run alone
forbidden_changes: modify files outside allowed_write_paths, including mike_trade/brokers/shadow/account.py and ledger.py
change PLAN_SKELETON.json or other planning artifacts
fill at candle close or any price not supported by quote evidence
import or call any Alpaca trading client, paper/live endpoint, or broker credential
use float for prices, quantities, or fees
create live broker orders or run broad test suites/backtests
